note: Design knowledge in our own words, distilled from user-curated references and the private library. Status levels: principle (documented), recipe (structured recipe exists), renderable (the engine draws it), tested (rendered and verified by an automated test). Private reference records link to these ids.

principles.rule: Action title: one conclusion sentence (≤16 words) in a heavy serif, at most two lines; it states a direction or rank the data support.
Exhibit header: a bold sans finding, the unit and period on the next line in regular weight, then a hairline rule before the evidence.
Type scale for 1280×720: title 30 pt, exhibit 14 pt, body 12.5 pt, axis 10.5 pt, data labels 11.5 pt, sources 8.5 pt; never below 8.5 pt.
Key figures in a large serif in the primary colour; supporting figures smaller in near-black; captions in sans.
Commentary as short blocks that open with a bold lead-in of two to four words; bold only the phrase that carries the point.
Sequences use large serif numerals (01–04) or numbered circles; outlined circles on light pages, filled on dark.
Caveat tags (Illustrative, Not exhaustive, Directional) set small and underlined beside the exhibit header.
principles.fallback: put the caveat in the unit line

principles.rule: Footnote system: superscript markers on labels with numbered notes above the source line.
principles.fallback: write the definition in the unit line

principles.rule: Label directly: series names and latest values at line ends, values at or inside bar ends; no legend when labels can carry it.
Highlight in grey: the focus entity in the primary colour, everything else one or two neutral tones; a second highlight tone only with a legend.
Donut with the share written large in serif in its centre; pairs of donuts side by side, each with its own small title.
principles.needs: a share between 0 and 100 with provenance
principles.fallback: figure with caption; never a donut for non-shares (debt ratios are not shares)

principles.rule: 100%-stacked horizontal bars by entity with category flags, segment values inside the segments, legend above in segment order.
principles.needs: shares that sum to 100 per entity

principles.rule: Stacked or grouped columns with totals above the stacks and segment values inside; the highlighted segment in the primary colour.
principles.needs: components that add to a total

principles.rule: Annotate inside the chart: a shaded period labelled with its years, one computed callout, gap brackets with their values, range arrows.
Two-period increment: the later column drawn on the earlier level with the increment in the primary colour and the change written large above.
Small multiples on one scale in a grid, grouped in labelled rows (e.g. advanced / emerging) with dashed separators; the focus entity's panel larger.
A benchmark bar (average, OECD, peer group) in neutral grey inside a ranked list, labelled as a benchmark.
principles.fallback: name the benchmark in the exhibit title

principles.rule: Flags beside entity names in rankings and lists; drawn as native shapes, not images.
Maps carry analysis: choropleth with a stepped legend, or proportional bubbles with value labels ('now (then)'), callout boxes with leader lines and trend icons.
Nested proportional shapes (circles or squares sized by value) compare two growth rates or a part within a whole; the ratio stated large.
Signed changes in pills aligned under the groups they describe, coloured by sign.
principles.fallback: change column in a ranked table

principles.rule: Sparklines in table cells share one window (stated in the header) and carry no end labels.
Stage-axis area charts (shares across a process, e.g. channels by purchase step) with in-area callouts.
Ranked table: rank, flag, entity, an in-cell bar of the latest value with its label, the earlier value and the change; focus row tinted; hairline rows.
Scorecard matrix: numbered rows per measure, focus and reference side by side, gap, change, sparkline and a computed reading; a conclusion row under a heavier rule.
principles.needs: several metrics for focus and peer

principles.rule: Two-level headers: a section header spanning its columns over the column headers, with rules at both levels; two tables side by side.
Metric rows aligned under a chart's groups (e.g. spend intent, change in spend), so the chart and its mini-table share x-positions.
Heatmap and indicator cells for scored comparisons, with the scale explained.
Benchmark list: flag, entity, earlier value, latest value (bold), change; focus row first and tinted.
White page with a light frame: no band; tracker in the primary colour above the title; sources at the foot.
Asymmetric columns (8/4, 7/5) with a full-height implications panel bleeding to the edge; the title keeps clear of it; a gold edge marks it.
principles.needs: columns with a tinted last column

principles.rule: Multi-module pages: two or three analytical modules, each with its own finding-led header, separated by hairline dividers.
Split background: a colour field holding the title (and a motif) beside white content; for summaries, closings and statements.
Summary-to-detail bracket: a bracket from a summary chart's segment to the detail table that explains it.
Join symbols between modules (+ for 'and', » for 'therefore') on the divider line.
The title as a design element: placed lower-left over a map or image on statement slides.
Background variety within one identity: white, ivory panels, ivory split fields, deep-wine dividers; dark full slides only for a few statements or maps.
Explanation cards coloured like the chart's series double as its legend.
Variety rule: consecutive slides use different compositions; the frame, type and colour roles stay constant.
Node-and-edge diagrams for ecosystems and transmission: nodes as cards or circles with their figure, edges as labelled arrows (words only).
Causal chains read left to right with one feedback edge routed under the row; label links as accounting links, not estimated effects.
Numbered journeys or stages along a path, alternating text left and right.
Radial frameworks: categories as arcs, levers as wedges, an axis of ambition; side-by-side versions with a highlighted outline compare plans.
Arrow-shaped banner headers (chevrons) title the two sides of a comparison.

Colour roles: white and warm ivory backgrounds; deep burgundy only for focal data, key figures and highlights; antique gold for hairlines, dividers and borders; near-black in small amounts; warm taupe for peers; never grey-heavy.
Thematic motifs: thin line art in gold, transparent, anchored to the foot of a panel or field, at most one per slide, decorative only.
Licensed imagery as duotone or cutout, cropped to a field or edge, never a plain rectangle across content; licence and attribution recorded in the picture's description and the source line.
Fine line-pattern geometry (fanning lines) as cover texture.
Context markers: a country flag or topic icon beside the title.
Three levels of message: the action title states the conclusion, exhibit headers state sub-findings, the panel states implications for the audience.
Then and now in one label ('13 (8)') or one row (2022, 2025, change).
A big ratio statement (~2x, +52%) anchors a page when the comparison is the message.
No figure repeated as a focal point on adjacent slides; each slide adds information.
Deck rhythm: agenda, numbered dividers, content; an executive summary up front.
Render each new slide and compare it with one or two retrieved references before accepting it.
Mechanical QA: no overflow, overlap or out-of-bounds; type ≥ 8.5 pt; integrity OK with no unsourced figures.
Colour discipline: the primary colour marks only focal data; gold only for structure; near-black only for titles and figures.
Deck-level checks: repeated focal figures, consecutive identical compositions.
